server.$comment: One connection per scenario, served with token, ide and version. authorize(path) answers authorizePrefix + path, or fails with authorizeRefuses[path]; the handler answers every call with answers[method], openDocument's with the path it was handed first, unless the scenario's handlerRefuses[method] makes it fail with that refusal. send: the pieces the peer writes, in order; before the next piece, and before the outcome is read, the reader waits until the hub is idle: every complete frame sent so far answered, refused or skipped, no handler call pending, and the connection read from again, ended or hung up (the TypeScript reader lets ten event-loop turns pass). expect: every frame the hub wrote, newline dropped. then: open, end (it ended the connection after its frames) or hangUp (it destroyed it). authorized: every path authorize was handed, in order, as the peer wrote it; a request whose params are refused never reaches authorize. calls: the handler calls in order, normalized: the path of a method that names one, create by JavaScript truthiness and initialValue when a string on openDocument, actions on applyActions, null otherwise, and the connection's client. logs: the texts the hub logged, in order.

authz.$comment: A machine per vector: realPath maps a path equal to a links key, or under it, onto the key's target and succeeds when that path exists, paths compared as strings, case included; only the first key that matches, in the order written, is followed, and only once, so a target under another key is not followed again; lstat finds an entry at a links key even when its target is missing, else where the followed path exists. existing: the paths that exist, each with every ancestor. failing: paths whose realPath fails for a reason other than a missing entry. resolve: resolveRealPath of target is real, null when no safe real path exists. authorize: authorizePath of target with folders and documents is real, or fails with error.
